relevance_note: One cohort patient (P10) carries a TNFAIP3 variant described individually: "A variant in the tumor necrosis factor, alpha-induced protein (TNFAIP)3 gene (c.997dupG) resulting in a frameshift (p.A333fs^*2) was found in P10".
method_note: WES study of 20 CVID patients; only P10 has a TNFAIP3 variant, so the other 19 patients are out of scope and counted in cohort_size_as_stated. P10's mother and father are included as relatives described in relation to P10, from the 'Predispositions' column of the fixed-width Supplementary Table S3 (row 10: 'mother: asthma, thyroiditis. Father: DMII'); the text of that cell is split over several lines, so spans quote its pieces; neither parent was reported as tested. Rows were built by a short Python script from my own reading; fixed-width supplementary segments (Table S2 row P10, Table S3 row 10 treatment columns, Table S4 row 10) were copied from the file and checked against the column headers by eye. Table S3 row 10 columns read as: pneumococcal antibodies NP, immunization test NP, FEV1 NP, faecal calprotectin 1266 (no reference value given, not recorded as a feature), microbiology sputum isolates, referred from unknown, prophylactic AB Sulfotrim, IVIG Hizentra. Zygosity 'heterozygous' for the TNFAIP3 variant comes from the Table 2 title 'Monoallelic variants identified' (rule 8: monoallelic); for the IL2RG variant from the Table S2 legend ('all variants are heterozygous except one homozygous variant found in P4'). The IL2RG c.-83G>A variant (Table S2, 'considered unlikely disease-causing') is recorded because it is attributed to P10 unambiguously and is rare, not a common SNP. Inheritance not reported: Table 3 says 'Unknown' and the text says the authors could not verify de novo vs inherited. No functional assay was done ('we were not able to functionally validate identified variants'), so functional_evidence_statement is 'not reported'. Cytopenias (anemia, thrombocytopenia, pancytopenia) are recorded as features but the checklist item 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' is 'not reported' because the paper does not call them autoimmune and links thrombocytopenia to hypersplenism. Splenomegaly/hepatosplenomegaly are not taken as 'lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy'. Mother's 'thyroiditis' is not stated to be autoimmune, so that checklist item is 'not reported'. Table 4 laboratory values were not converted into features against the reference ranges except IgA 'BD' (defined as below detection limit); IgM for P10 is '^*' (no measurement). The 'markedly reduced isotype-switched memory B cells' row is inferred from the statement naming P15 as the only exception. Study inclusion criteria (decreased IgG/IgM/IgA) were not used as evidence. The paper says the Danish CVID cohort was described before (refs 2, 8) but does not say these 20 patients were individually described, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null. Age at diagnosis '23' is the Table 1 'Age at diagnosis' column (unit not printed; years assumed for the ISO value). No stacked ' / ' cells involved P10. No contradictions found concerning P10.
